topic: The Inscribed Square Problem: Can You Find a Square on Any Loop?
target_audience: Undergraduate students and advanced high school mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: The Hook: Shapey the Snail’s Trail
lecture_lines: A snail crawls in a messy, closed loop.
Can we find four points forming a square?
This is the classic "Square Peg Problem".
animations: Draw a complex, non-self-intersecting loop in purple (#A020F0).
A yellow (#FFFF00) square frame moves around, its corners trying to touch the loop.
The words "Square Peg Problem" appear in white (#FFFFFF) at the bottom.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Jordan Curves
lecture_lines: These loops are formally known as Jordan curves.
They are simple, closed, and never cross themselves.
We can stretch them into any "blob" shape.
animations: Label the purple loop "Jordan Curve" in white (#FFFFFF).
A white dot (#FFFFFF) travels around the loop to demonstrate it is simple and closed.
Smoothly morph the loop into a green (#00FF00) jagged blob.

sections.title: The Strategy: From Square to Rectangle
lecture_lines: Proving a square exists is a hard challenge.
Instead, let's look for an inscribed rectangle first.
Rectangles have two equal diagonals sharing a midpoint.
animations: Show the green blob; place four points on it that clearly don't form a square.
A cyan (#00FFFF) rectangle appears and its corners snap onto the green blob.
Draw two orange (#FF8C00) diagonals within the rectangle, crossing at a white (#FFFFFF) midpoint.

sections.title: The Configuration Space: Mapping Pairs
lecture_lines: We map every pair of points to 3D space.
Height represents the distance between the points.
The base coordinates represent their unique midpoint.
Moving points along the loop creates a surface.
This "configuration space" captures all possible pairings.
animations: Place two red (#FF0000) points on the loop; draw a line connecting them.
From the midpoint of the red line, draw a vertical green (#00FF00) vector whose length equals the distance between the red points.
Show the midpoint M (#FFFFFF) on the loop's plane as the base of the vector.
As red points move, the green vector's tip traces a blue (#0000FF) "canopy" shape above the loop's plane.
Label the blue shape "Configuration Space" in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Topological Twist: The Möbius Strip
lecture_lines: Unordered pairs on a loop form a Möbius strip.
It's a surface with only one side.
The boundary of this strip is our original loop.
We glue the edges with a topological twist.
This realization is the key to the proof.
animations: Show a rectangular strip (#00BFFF) with a "twist" animation.
Color one side of the strip red (#FF0000) and trace its continuous surface.
Highlight the single edge of the Möbius strip in purple (#A020F0) to match the original loop.
Animate the "gluing" of the ends with a 180-degree flip.
The text "Key Realization" flashes in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Conclusion: The Intersection Proof
lecture_lines: A Möbius strip must intersect itself in 3D.
At the intersection, two distinct pairs overlap.
They share a midpoint and have equal length.
These four points form the corners of a rectangle.
We have found our inscribed shape on the loop!
animations: Display a 2D projection of a Möbius strip (#00BFFF) showing a point where the surface crosses itself.
Highlight the intersection point with a pulsing yellow (#FFFF00) glow.
From the intersection point, extract two line segments of equal length and common midpoint.
Project these segments back onto the original loop to form a cyan (#00FFFF) rectangle.
The rectangle corners flash, indicating the problem is solved for rectangles.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Status
lecture_lines: Rectangles exist for all smooth Jordan curves.
For fractal-like loops, the square version remains open.
Mathematics still has many beautiful mysteries to solve.
animations: Show a smooth curve with a cyan (#00FFFF) rectangle inside.
Show a fractal curve with a yellow (#FFFF00) question mark.
Display the names "Vaughan" and "Stromquist" in white (#FFFFFF), then fade to black.
